highlights.body:
**Settings → Changelog.** The Changelog tab in Settings now lists what's new in skill-map: one entry per release, newest first, bullet points for the user-facing changes plus the workspace(s) each change affected. The same content is bundled with the demo so it's available offline too. The tab populates automatically on every release.

**Project DB path.** The "Project DB" row in Settings → About now shows the path relative to your project folder (`.skill-map/skill-map.db`) instead of repeating the absolute prefix already shown in the row above. Cleaner, less redundant.

**Tags zoom-to-matching.** Clicking a tag chip in the inspector now pans + zooms the graph to fit every node that carries the tag. Click the same chip again to clear the selection and return to the previous view. The chip itself lights up to show what's filtering — an active tag is unmistakable in the panel.

**Bump sidecars in batch.** New `sm bump --pending` walks every node whose `.sm` sidecar reports drift (body or frontmatter hash mismatch) and refreshes them in one pass — bumps `annotations.version`, recomputes hashes, stamps `audit.lastBumpedAt` / `lastBumpedBy`. Single-node `sm bump <path>` also lands. The CLI surface mirrors the on-disk write.

**Annotation catalog now 14 fields.** Dropped `released` (redundant with `audit.lastBumpedAt`). The inspector and node card now read the activity timestamp from the reserved `audit:` block — no more confusion between "officially released" and "last bumped".

**View contribution system.** Plugins can now contribute slot-aware visuals to the inspector and the graph card without being wired by hand: per-node counters, alerts, key-value rows. Two built-ins ship today: `core/external-url-counter` (counts external URLs per node) and `core/link-counts` (in / out link counters).

**Multi-provider support.** The kernel registry is now open per Provider — Claude, Gemini, and the open-standard `agent-skills` flavour all coexist. Cards paint with each Provider's accent; the kind palette in the graph view filters on the actual node kind names rather than a closed enum.
